# Convert WebM to MP4

- Route: `/tools/convert-webm-to-mp4`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `video`
- Slug: `convert-webm-to-mp4`

## Summary

Turn web-optimized .webm video into an MP4 you can edit, share, and play on any device. (Video tools)

## Details

WebM is a modern, open container built for the web — small files, great for browser video. But many video editors, older devices, and messaging apps cannot open WebM. Converting WebM to MP4 re-encodes the VP8/VP9 video to H.264 and the audio to AAC, giving you a file that works in Premiere, Resolve, phones, and TVs.
### What it does
- Converts .webm (VP8/VP9 + Vorbis/Opus) video to MP4.
- Locks the output to MP4 (H.264 + AAC) for maximum compatibility.
- Adds yuv420p and +faststart so the MP4 plays in every browser and starts instantly.
- A WebM screen capture can be trimmed or resized on its way to MP4.
### How to use it
1. Upload your WebM: Drop in a .webm file downloaded from the web or a screen recorder.
2. Output is locked to MP4: MP4 is preset for this tool — nothing to configure.
3. Convert: We transcode VP8/VP9 to H.264 + AAC.
4. Download: Save your MP4 for editing or playback anywhere.
### Supported formats
- Input: webm
- Output: mp4
- Output is locked to MP4 (H.264 + AAC, yuv420p, +faststart).
### Technical details
- WebM uses VP8/VP9 video, which most editors cannot import; MP4/H.264 imports cleanly into every NLE.
- We force yuv420p so the MP4 plays in Safari and on social platforms.
- If you actually want a smaller web file, the reverse MP4-to-WebM tool produces VP9 WebM instead.
### Use cases
- Edit downloaded video: Bring a .webm clip into Premiere or Resolve as an MP4.
- Screen recordings: Convert a WebM screen capture into a shareable MP4.
- Play on older devices: Make a WebM file play on a TV or phone that does not support it.
- Messaging apps: Send video to apps that accept MP4 but not WebM.
### FAQ
Q: How do I convert WebM to MP4?
A: Upload your .webm file and click convert — the output is already set to MP4.
Q: Why can my editor not open WebM?
A: Most editors do not include VP8/VP9 import. Converting to MP4 (H.264) fixes the import.
Q: Will the file get bigger?
A: MP4/H.264 can be slightly larger than VP9 WebM at the same quality. Pick a lower quality preset if size matters.
Q: Does it keep the audio?
A: Yes — Vorbis/Opus audio is re-encoded to AAC and stays in sync.
